01

Setting specification

Task

Output a unit vector approximating the leading eigenspace of $A$.

Admissible model

Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$, $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, $0<\lambda_1(A)\le\Lambda$, $\lambda_1(A)-\lambda_2(A)\ge\gamma\lambda_1(A)$, and $0<\gamma\le1$. If $d=1$, use the convention $\lambda_2=0$. The leading eigendirection is unique.

Oracle interface

The information $d,\gamma,\Lambda,\varepsilon,\delta$ is public. The matrix $A$ and its eigenvectors are hidden. Query $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$; the actual largest eigenvalue is not additionally disclosed.

Output

Return any unit vector $\widehat v\in\mathbb R^d$, without a certificate.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Let $u_1$ be any unit basis of the true leading eigenspace. The base loss is $1-|u_1^{\mathsf T}\widehat{v}|^2$, with success threshold $\varepsilon^2$; sign changes do not affect the loss.

Resource accounting

Count right products with single vectors only: $N=N_{\mathrm r}$. A block of width $q$ costs $q$ calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least $1-\delta$.

Budget convention
fixed worst-case joint budget; no expectation substituted

B1

Random-start Lanczos with Chebyshev-filter analysis, or deterministic reconstruction

Local argument in this profile · see complete PDF / LaTeX ↗
Algorithm scope
Both deterministic algorithms and algorithms with private randomness are permitted. Queries may depend on the entire response history. Query vectors are unrestricted; no Krylov, span, or zero-respecting condition is imposed. Storage, exact-real computation, and communication have no additional constraints. Parallel block calls are still charged by column.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Positive universal constants, permitted to depend on any explicitly fixed auxiliary parameters.
Derivation
Draw the initial vector $g_0\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, both $|u_1^{\mathsf T}g_0|\ge c\delta$ and $\|g_0\|_2\le C\sqrt{d/\delta}$ hold. Choose a scaled Chebyshev polynomial $P_t$ of degree at most $t$ such that $P_t(\lambda_1)=1$ and $\max_{x\in[0,\lambda_2]}|P_t(x)|\le2\exp(-ct\sqrt\gamma)$; if $\lambda_2=0$, one matrix application suffices. The vector $P_t(A)g_0$ lies in the Krylov subspace, and the sine of its angle to $u_1$ is at most $C\sqrt d\,\delta^{-3/2}\exp(-ct\sqrt\gamma)$. The unit vector maximizing the Rayleigh quotient in that subspace has no greater Rayleigh loss. By $\lambda_1-\lambda_2\ge\gamma\lambda_1$, dividing the normalized Rayleigh loss by $\gamma$ bounds the squared sine error. Thus $t=O\!\bigl(\gamma^{-1/2}\log(Cd/(\delta\varepsilon\gamma))\bigr)$ suffices. The unknown values $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ are used only to prove the existence of the polynomial; the algorithm need not know them. The projected matrix is formed from the queried Krylov vectors. Alternatively, $d$ standard-basis queries reconstruct the matrix exactly.
Comparison argument
An upper bound is verified on the general (epsilon,delta,gamma,d) domain. The lower bound applies only in the specific window listed next.
R2Optimal

The matching strip relating angular accuracy to the spectral gap.

Parameter region
Assume $0<\gamma\le1/14$, $\delta=1/10$, $\gamma^2\le\varepsilon^2\le\gamma/12$, and $d\ge\max\{D_0(\gamma),\gamma^{-2}\}$. The quantity $D_0$ is the sufficient polynomial dimension threshold in SER18.
Success guarantee
Choose one algorithm, then require success probability at least $1-\delta$ on every fixed admissible input, over the algorithm’s private randomness. The input is independent of the private seed. Average correctness under an input distribution is insufficient.
Quantity
Q1

B2

Randomly rotated spiked-Wigner hard instances, affinely transformed to positive semidefinite matrices.

Tight Query Complexity Lower Bounds for PCA via Finite Sample Deformed Wigner Law ↗
Algorithm scope
Both deterministic algorithms and algorithms with private randomness are permitted. Queries may depend on the entire response history. Query vectors are unrestricted; no Krylov, span, or zero-respecting condition is imposed. Storage, exact-real computation, and communication have no additional constraints. Parallel block calls are still charged by column.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Positive universal constants, permitted to depend on any explicitly fixed auxiliary parameters.
Derivation
Use the rank-one hard instance from Theorem 2.2 of Simchowitz, El Alaoui, and Recht (2018). Set its asymptotic relative gap to $h=7\gamma\le1/2$ and choose $\lambda>1$ so that $s=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}=2/(1-h)$. The source matrix is $M=W+\lambda u_0u_0^{\mathsf T}$, where $W$ is its normalized Gaussian symmetric noise matrix and $u_0$ is the hidden unit vector. On the source event $E_{\mathrm{good}}(1/2)$, we have $\lambda_1(M)\le3s/2$ and $\lambda_1(M)-\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge(s-2)/2=hs/2$, hence $\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le s+1$. Setting $B=M+2sI_d$ gives $B\succ0$, $\lambda_1(B)\le7s/2$, and relative leading-eigenvalue gap at least $h/7=\gamma$. Then $A=(2\Lambda/(7s))B$ ensures $\lambda_1(A)\le\Lambda$. The matrices $A$ and $M$ have the same leading eigenvector; each $A$ product is simulated by exactly one $M$ query and public linear operations. If the squared sine error is at most $\varepsilon^2\le h/12$, the output has Rayleigh quotient for $|M|=(M^2)^{1/2}$ at least $(1-h/12)\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, meeting the source theorem's target. The theorem therefore excludes unrestricted randomized adaptive algorithms using fewer than $ch^{-1/2}\log d$ queries. The sufficient dimension threshold $D_0(\gamma)$ retains the polynomial conditions in Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 6.1 and the condition making the failure bound a constant; unspecified constants remain unspecified. In the region $\delta=1/10$, $\gamma^2\le\varepsilon^2\le\gamma/12$, and $d\ge\max\{D_0(\gamma),\gamma^{-2}\}$, all additional upper-bound logarithms are controlled by $\log d$, giving $\Theta(\gamma^{-1/2}\log d)$.
Upper bound
\[O(\gamma^{-1/2}\log d)\]
